e07726c468.why: No longer the same fact as the diver item: it now keys the grade 5 syringe evidence that an 'empty' syringe holds air, which takes up space (Horizon ASSET: a finger on the tip, the plunger goes in only part way; Inquiry Project Grade 5 Inv. 13: 'air clearly takes up space'). Lures are truly wrong: with the tip open the plunger slides all the way, and a sealed push raises the pressure, so there is no suction. 'Looks empty' and 'trapped' are mild hints but are the standard set-up. The particle-spacing explanation is left to T2.

0bfbadd6c7.why: Wording fixed ('It has turned into more water'; 'a scoop of salt'), and the telling-materials-apart twin is re-keyed. Key true (Grokipedia Sodium chloride: Na+ and Cl- ions separate from the lattice; 360 g per kg, so a scoop dissolves fully). Salt melts at 800.7 C; the salt is still there and returns when the water evaporates. Lead note: the mixtures-and-solutions draft's copper sulfate item keys almost the same fact ('Spread evenly all through the water'), to settle when that unit is judged.

19e2ab5a75.why: The 'iron' answer is gone: the stem now asks about structure ('What is the steel like, deep inside?'), and the four choices fit it. Key true (Wikipedia Atom: about 100 pm; atoms cannot be seen with conventional microscopes). The continuous-matter, air-in-the-gaps and magnifying-glass lures are truly wrong. Three choices begin 'Particles', but each half of the contest needs real knowledge (size, empty gaps), and 'one solid piece' is the documented misconception.
